text:
incident-bot: ALERT — autoscaler ceiling hit for nodepool prod-gpu-standard (us-west-2). Unable to scale above max_nodes=24. Queue: generation-requests q=1.9k (+350% in 10m), avg token latency +420ms. P95 generation time increased. Paging ops-oncall.

ops-oncall: received. jumping in. tagging @sanjay @lia. any active deploys? :eyes: 

sanjay: no deploys on prod. seeing spike in batch inference traffic from embedder-job and a few customers. Autoscaler events show "no capacity left in region" and kube events show failed provisioning from cloud API (quota?).

lia: checking cloud console + infra quotas. gcloud shows GPU quota at limit for that project: GPUs: 24/24. There was an emergency burst earlier that consumed extra GPUs in the shared pool.

ops-oncall: ok. so autoscaler can't request more because cloud quota hard cap. can we borrow from another pool or spin up a different sku?

charles: cross-pool borrowing would be manual. We have a spare nodepool prod-gpu-preempt (preemptible) with quota available but pod tolerations may not match. Preemptible risk is higher but we can route non-critical traffic.

eva: support notes — two customers (acct-phi, acct-ml-uptime) reported degraded responses. SLA alerts fired 10m ago. ETA on mitigation important for paging.

kube-bot: Events: Deployment/embeddings: "0/24 nodes available: insufficient gpu." ClusterAutoscaler: "Max nodes reached for nodegroup prod-gpu-standard: maxNodes=24"

sanjay: quick plan: 1) Attempt manual cap raise in cloud quota (request immediate quota increase) 2) Temporarily cordon some low-priority pods and reschedule to preemptible pool 3) Patch autoscaler maxNodes to 40 for prod-gpu-standard as emergency override — manual approval required.

lia: I can request an emergency quota bump via support console but that takes 30-90m normally. We have an internal emergency path: charles, can you approve in cloud org for a manual quota override?

charles: I can. Approving temporary GPU quota raise to 48 for project rw-prod-ml. Applying now. (reacted with :white_check_mark:)

ops-oncall: while that propagates, let's do the quicker routing change. Which pods are safe to move? sanjay, can you run a pod priority list?

sanjay: listing top consumers and priorities...

sanjay: (paste)
```
kubectl get pods -n production -o=custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,PRIORITY:.spec.priorityClassName,NODE:.spec.nodeName --sort-by=.spec.priority
# embeddings-worker-1   high     node-07
# realtime-gen-2        critical  node-03
# batch-embed-5         low      node-12
```

sanjay: We can evict batch-embed pods (low). Lia, can you taint the preemptible pool to accept these with tolerations? I'll patch deployment tolerations.

lia: done. added toleration and nodeSelector on a canary deployment for batch-embed. rolling update triggered.

ops-oncall: immediate effect on queue?

sanjay: queue dropped to 1.2k in 6m. latencies starting to improve. But still above target. Manual autoscaler patch next. We need a COA for risk: if we bump maxNodes to 40, provisioning could take 6-12m per node; cost impact high. Are we ok with cost to restore SLAs?

eva: from SRE support: customers told us to prioritize availability over cost for now. They want updates every 15m.

charles: approving manual autoscaler override for emergency. I'm granting terraform patch permission to sanjay for the change.

sanjay: applying patch to cluster-autoscaler config:
```bash
kubectl -n kube-system patch configmap autoscaler-config --patch '\n{"data":{"prod-gpu-standard.maxNodes":"40"}}'\n
```

sanjay: running now. (reacted with :rocket:)

kube-bot: ClusterAutoscaler: 'Scaling up: requesting 12 nodes for nodegroup prod-gpu-standard (desired 36)'. Cloud provider API: provisioning started.

ops-oncall: monitoring node join events. ETA on first new nodes?

lia: first new node joined in 90s, then more. GPU quota increase shows applied.

sanjay: pods starting to schedule onto new nodes. queue now 420, P95 latency improving toward normal.

eva: telling customers: "We're actively adding capacity and reducing a backlog caused by an autoscaler limit. Expecting near-normal service within 15-30 minutes. Apologies for the disruption."

ops-oncall: confirming all critical queues drained to acceptable thresholds. any residual error rates?

sanjay: error spike resolved, 200->~0.5% over baseline. Monitoring for any regressions.

charles: good work. immediate postmortem owners: sanjay to lead investigation into why GPU quota was exhausted (burst control), lia to follow up on autoscaler hard max detection and alerting, ops-oncall to update runbook to include preemptible fallback automation.

ops-oncall: follow-ups and timeline: - 0-30m: mitigation complete (nodes added, queues drained) - 30-180m: monitor and verify stability - 24h: incident review + corrective actions assigned

sanjay: captured runbook snippets used (for postmortem):
```
# emergency autoscaler override
kubectl -n kube-system get configmap autoscaler-config -o yaml > /tmp/a.yaml
# edit maxNodes for nodegroup prod-gpu-standard to 40
kubectl -n kube-system apply -f /tmp/a.yaml
# note: also request cloud quota bump in parallel
```

lia: logging this under INC-2376543210 and adding tags: autoscaler, gpu-quota, manual-cap-raise.

ops-oncall: closing loop: does anyone need further action in channel?

eva: support will follow up with customers and close tickets after postmortem.

charles: I'll revert the manual override after we confirm stability (target: revert to safe baseline maxNodes=24 and implement automated safeguards).

ops-oncall: thanks team. I'll update the incident timeline in PagerDuty and schedule the postmortem meeting. :thumbsup:
